title: What if every human vanished?
hook: What if every human vanished today?
camera: locked high three-quarter aerial view of a low-poly city crossroads: a wide intersection with cars, a subway entrance with stairs in the lower left, tall glass skyscrapers on both sides, a steel suspension bridge over a river in the far right distance, two power plant cooling towers on the far horizon, open sky across the top third left free for titles
cta: Which building would last the longest?

beats.caption: 8 billion people, gone
beats.vo: What if every human vanished today? All eight billion of us, in one second.
beats.state: bright midday, cars stopped in the middle of the intersection with doors open, traffic lights lit, shop windows lit, no people anywhere
beats.fact_source: UN World Population Prospects 2024: about 8.2 billion people

beats.caption: The subway floods
beats.vo: Day two. The power is out, so New York's subway pumps stop. Thirteen million gallons a day now flood the tunnels.
beats.state: grey overcast day, every window and traffic light dark, water pouring up out of the subway entrance and spreading across the street
beats.fact_source: MTA: subway pumps remove about 13 million gallons of water a day; Alan Weisman, The World Without Us (2007)

beats.caption: Wait, don't reactors explode?
beats.vo: Wait, don't nuclear plants explode? Not like bombs. But with no one cooling them, many of the four hundred reactors melt down.
beats.state: hazy orange dusk, thin plumes of smoke rising from the two cooling towers on the horizon, the flooded street shining, birds on the cars
beats.fact_source: IAEA PRIS: about 415 operational power reactors in 2024; Weisman, The World Without Us

beats.caption: Weeds break the asphalt
beats.vo: Year one. Weeds push through every crack in the asphalt. Deer walk down the empty avenue.
beats.state: fresh spring morning, green weeds and grass in every crack of the road, dusty cars with flat tires, two deer standing in the middle of the intersection
beats.fact_source: Weisman, The World Without Us: freeze-thaw cycles crack pavement within the first winters

beats.caption: Trees grow through cars
beats.vo: Year twenty. Trees grow straight through the cars. Vines climb the towers and windows start to fall out.
beats.state: summer, young trees growing through rusting cars, the road covered in grass, green vines on the skyscraper walls, many broken windows
beats.fact_source: Weisman, The World Without Us; History Channel, Life After People (2008)

beats.caption: Skyscrapers start falling
beats.vo: Year one hundred. Steel rusts from the inside. The first skyscrapers lean, crack and fall.
beats.state: autumn, dense forest filling the streets, one skyscraper collapsed into rubble, another leaning with its top broken, brown rust streaks on the remaining towers
beats.fact_source: Life After People (2008): unmaintained steel-frame buildings fail within decades to centuries

beats.caption: The bridge snaps
beats.vo: Year three hundred. The great steel bridge finally snaps and drops into the river.
beats.state: stormy grey day, the suspension bridge broken in the middle with its deck fallen into the river, most skyscrapers reduced to stumps covered in trees
beats.fact_source: Weisman, The World Without Us: large steel bridges fall within about 300 years

beats.caption: Only stone remains
beats.vo: Ten thousand years later, only stone and glass remain. [pause 0.4] And it all started today, when every human vanished.
beats.state: golden sunset, a lush forest and a meadow where the city stood, a few moss-covered stone ruins, the bridge and cooling towers gone, a herd of wild horses grazing
beats.fact_source: Weisman, The World Without Us: stone, glass, bronze and plastics outlast everything else
